title: Designing for Thumbs
intro: Design for the centre and the edges differently. Space targets more at the top and bottom.

learn.title: Grips
learn.text:
Of 780 people touching their phones: **49% one hand, 36% cradled, 15% two hands.**

Grips change every few seconds, so reach zones aren’t fixed.

try.q: About what share used one hand?

learn.title: Accuracy by zone
learn.text:
**Centre:** most accurate.
**Left and right:** slightly less, same for both hands.
**Top and bottom:** least accurate, slowest, least confident.

try.explain: Release-based taps drift at low thumb angles.

learn.title: Spacing in millimetres
learn.text:
**Centre:** about **7 mm** apart.
**Top and bottom:** **10–12 mm** between items.
**Sides:** full-width list rows over small icons and checkboxes.

try.q: Targets in a bottom bar should be spaced about:

learn.title: Practical rules
learn.text:
Keep tappable items away from tab bars.
Leave room below the last list item.
Check smaller screens.
Test on a real device in every grip.

try.q: Why leave room below the last list item?
options: So people can scroll it to a better spot

test.q: Hoober’s later advice on thumb-reach drawings:
How should rare or risky actions be placed?
options: Not in hard-to-hit edges just for reach

test.q: Which is the better side-of-screen control?
Misses near the bottom bar. Often the best fix?
How many people were observed in total?
test.explain: 780 of them were touching the screen.

test.q: What should you check on smaller phones?
test.explain: A bar of five icons may fit only four.
